doc:
/**
 * Week 1 — the foundations a Bengali speaker needs before anything else.
 *
 * The rule families introduced here are the ones that decide most English
 * spellings a learner will meet in the first fortnight: doubling before a vowel
 * suffix, dropping a silent e, y to i, the -es plural, a/an, the ck/tch/dge
 * spellings after a short vowel, the floss doubling, q always taking u, and no
 * English word ending in v.
 *
 * The vocabulary is high-frequency first — `frequencyRank` drives the order
 * within a day — and every `commonMisspellings` entry is an error a Bengali
 * speaker actually produces rather than a random corruption: `dis` for `this`
 * and `tink` for `think` from the missing dental fricatives, `vil` for `will`
 * and `bhery` for `very` from the missing /v/ and /w/, `recieve` and `beleive`
 * from the i-before-e rule itself.
 *
 * IPA is the standard British reference accent, which is what
 * `learner_profiles.accent_preference` defaults to.
 */

days.title: First words
days.focus: The commonest words in English, and the sounds Bangla does not have: /v/, /w/, /θ/ and /ð/.

days.title: Around the house
days.focus: Everyday nouns, the a/an rule, and the short-vowel ck spelling.

days.title: People and family
days.focus: Family words, subject-verb agreement, and the -es plural.

days.title: Doubling and dropping
days.focus: Double the final consonant before a vowel suffix; drop the silent e before one.

days.title: Y becomes I
days.focus: Consonant plus y turns to i before a suffix — happier, carried, cities.

days.title: Soft c and soft g
days.focus: Why c sounds like s and g like j before e, i and y, and the tch and dge spellings.

days.title: I before E, and no final V
days.focus: The i-before-e rule with its real exceptions, and why no English word ends in v.
